text:
maria-support: Escalation from ACME: multiple customers calls to function `create_order` are returning 422/400 "invalid arguments" and their bill spiked. Can we triage? :wave:

acme-infra: Seeing ~12% of requests failing since ~09:10 UTC. Error body: `{
  "error": "invalid_function_arguments",
  "details": "items: expected array, got string"
}`

maria-support: Thanks — @jess-ml can you take a look? Customer provided sample request and minimal repro. They say it started after they updated their client lib.

jess-ml: I pulled the sample. The customer is sending `items` as a JSON-encoded string rather than an array. Example payload they posted:

```json
{
  "action": "create_order",
  "user_id": 83422,
  "items": "[{\"sku\":\"WIDGET-1\",\"qty\":2}]",
  "metadata": "{\"source\":\"mobile\"}"
}
```

jess-ml: Our function signature expects `items: array<object>` and `metadata: object`. Because `items` is a string, our structured-output parser rejects it (strict schema enforcement).

acme-infra: That matches our logs — sample request (truncated): `POST /v1/invoke -> payload length=512, items type=string`

sam-sre: Also seeing a latency bump on those requests (p95 +480ms) — parser spends extra time attempting to coerce types before bailing. Correlates with the error rate.

jess-ml: Quick repro curl for the same bad payload:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"action":"create_order","user_id":83422,"items":"[{\"sku\":\"WIDGET-1\",\"qty\":2}]"}'
```

jess-ml: Root cause looks like ACME's client started double-encoding nested objects when `autoStringifyNested=true` in their SDK. Two mitigation options: (1) ask customer to turn that off / patch their client, (2) server-side tolerant parsing that tries JSON.parse on string fields that match JSON array/object patterns before strict validation.

leo-eng: Prefer safe server-side guard for SDK regressions: attempt a single JSON.parse on any string-valued arg when the declared schema expects array/object, but only when the string size < 64k and starts with `[` or `{`. Add strict logging and a feature flag.

maria-support: ACME can patch quickly but asked if Redwood can accept these benignly for now since rollout is org-wide. Customer is blocked for their release.

jess-ml: I can put a small tolerant-parser PR up today behind a flag. Will add a warning in the logs so we can rollback if it causes issues.

deploy-bot: deploy event: infra-config 2026-03-17T09:00:00Z by ops-deploy (id=2114999000) — no function runtime changes recorded.

sam-sre: FYI billing team flagged an unusual token/compute spike for that account; probably retries after 4xx are being retried by client. Recommend a temporary quota exemption while we triage.

maria-support: Action items:
- @acme-infra: try disabling `autoStringifyNested` and confirm (if they can patch now) :eyes:
- @jess-ml / @leo-eng: small tolerant-parse PR behind flag and canary it on a single shard
- @sam-sre: open billing exception for ACME (ticket #INC-21150)

acme-infra: Will try patch now and report back in 30m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Marking as escalated — will follow up with timeline and patch notes once jess deploys canary.
